properties.title: Stable Long-Horizon Neural ODE Reduced-Order Models via Learned Feedback for Biological Growth and Remodeling

membership.reason: Closed-loop hybrid mechanistic-learned Neural ODE reduced-order world model predicting long-horizon tissue deformation and mechanobiological growth conditioned on inflation protocol.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 protocol-conditioned hybrid biomechanical world model (WT_ORGAN, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: POD (r=9) + 2-layer Neural ODE + mechanistic growth field update + 4-layer CNN feedback encoder (Model D)

properties.flow: POD latent state z_k + volume setpoint protocol + CNN growth feedback g_k -> NODE Forward Euler rollout -> full skin displacement & area gain

properties.purpose: Rapid pre-operative surrogate simulation of skin tissue expansion growth and remodeling.
properties.environment: In silico Abaqus finite-element simulation benchmark (idealized skin geometry)

assertions.rationale: POD projection for displacement field (r=9) plus lightweight 4-layer CNN encoding mechanobiological growth fields into R^16.
Persistent augmented latent displacement/volume state z_k coupled with stored growth fields lambda^g_1, lambda^g_2.
Prescribed expander inflation volume setpoint protocol S_V(t_k) and PI controller error terms.
Continuous-time Neural ODE integrated with Forward Euler (Delta t = 1.4 days) over full expansion horizon.
Hybrid mechanistic-learned system: learned NODE latent velocity + mechanistic continuum growth equations.

Conditioned at every Forward Euler step on the prescribed inflation volume setpoint protocol S_V(t_k) and PI controller terms across Latin-hypercube-sampled final volumes Vf in [100, 700] mL; evaluated across 185 held-out Abaqus FE validation protocols (Model D captures 90.3% within clinical area-gain tolerance vs 43.7% open-loop).
Multiplicative finite growth split F = F^e F^g and mechanobiological stretch-rate ODEs.
Couples Neural ODE latent mechanics with explicit FE-style mechanobiological growth field updates.
Long-horizon tail loss L_tail penalizing smooth L1 rollout error over final 30% of trajectory.

Table 3 (p.16) reports best validation one-step latent MSE loss across all four models on the 185 validation simulations (Model D: 1.14e-3, Model B: 1.29e-3, Model C: 1.39e-3, Model A: 1.56e-3), in addition to full-horizon autoregressive rollout RMSE.
Rapid surrogate modeling for pre-operative tissue expansion protocol design.
Long-horizon rollout accuracy vs Abaqus FE ground truth: 90.3% validation cases within clinical tolerance (vs 43.7% open-loop).
Achieves >20,000x speedup over full finite-element Abaqus simulations.
Displacement dynamics integrated in 9-mode POD latent space.

evidence_fragments.content:
(G&R) remain largely unexplored. Here, we present a Neural Ordinary Differen-
tial Equation (NODE) ROM framework that learns latent dynamics of coupled
mechanical deformation and tissue growth, demonstrated in the context of skin
growth during tissue expansion (TE). TE is a challenging problem involving
nonlinear contact, history-dependent material behavior, and mechanobiologically
driven growth. The displacement field is compressed via Proper Orthogonal
Decomposition (POD) into a low-dimensional latent space, and a NODE learns
the resulting dynamics conditioned on patient-specific parameters. To address
long-horizon error accumulation, a key challenge in autoregressive latent dynam-
ical models, we propose a closed-loop architecture in which encoded features of
the evolving growth field are fed back into the dynamics at each step. We compare
feedback representations of increasing expressiveness: scalar, linear POD-based,
and nonlinear CNN-based. The CNN-based growth feature feedback substantially
stabilizes long-horizon rollouts. The best model captures 90.3% of validation cases
within clinical tolerance based on the final skin area gain, compared to 43.7%
for the open-loop baseline. Moreover, the NODE ROM achieves over 20000×
the speed of full finite element simulations. More broadly, these results suggest

3.2 Closed-Loop NODE Predictors with Growth Feature
Feedback
Anticipating model drift from open loop tissue growth ROMs, we introduce a closed-
loop NODE predictor architecture that modifies the open-loop predictor with a
feedback signal to the NODE from the current growth state. This structure more
closely mimics the coupled FE solver update for mechanics and growth than the
open-loop predictor, which evolves the displacement without any embedded growth
information. To create this structure, we modify the NODE input structure to pass
an additional input, a growth encodinggwith dimensionalityd g (Figure 7b).
The closed-loop architecture is detailed in Figure 8. At the start of the forward
iteration, the current reduced displacement statez k is decoded via the POD basis
into the full displacement fieldu k. Using this displacement field, the growth fieldsλ g
1,

geometry. The updated growth fields are passed to an operatorGwhich computes
an encoded representation of the growth fieldsgthat is passed to the NODE as a
closed-loop feedback signal.

locator.section_or_table: Section 2: Staged volume inflation protocol (Vf in [100, 700] mL)

evidence_fragments.content:
During simulation, we impose a staged volume inflation profile to inflate the expander
over time in increments of 100 mL as needed to achieve a final volume sampled between
Vf ∈[100 mL,700 mL]. The volume protocol is controlled by imposing a pressure load
via a proportional-integral (PI) controller with controller gains fixed to beK p = 1.0,
KI = 1.0, which allows sampled volume profiles to share a common trajectory before
fanning out to a specifiedV f (Figure 2).

capability_assessments.rationale: Protocol-conditioned hybrid mechanistic-learned Neural ODE surrogate simulating long-horizon tissue deformation and growth under prescribed inflation schedules (L2).

limitations: Trained and validated solely on idealized 300x300x3 mm square Abaqus FE simulations; no patient-specific clinical 3D photo validation.

legacy_cells.B: Stable Long-Horizon Neural ODE Reduced-Order Models via Learned Feedback for Biological Growth and Remodeling
legacy_cells.O: Skin deformation, growth and remodeling during tissue expansion (TE)
legacy_cells.S: Can a reduced-order Neural ODE model predict skin deformation and growth during tissue expansion across simulated volume protocols and parameters?
legacy_cells.AI: Synthetic finite-element simulation data; displacement fields; expander volume; principal growth-stretch fields; controller and material/growth parameters
legacy_cells.AJ: POD basis for displacement; fully connected Neural ODE; growth-field encoders compared: scalar area gain, POD, and CNN
legacy_cells.AM: Concatenated displacement POD coefficients and expander volume form the latent state; controller/material/growth inputs and growth encoding are supplied to the fully connected Neural ODE.
legacy_cells.AS: 10-dimensional augmented latent state (9 displacement POD coefficients plus expander volume)
legacy_cells.AT: Forward-Euler integration of the Neural ODE latent state; growth fields are updated at each step using the mechanistic growth equations and, for feedback variants, re-encoded into the transition.
legacy_cells.BD: Expander volume setpoint/protocol; staged inflation in 100 mL increments; final volume 100–700 mL; controller volume error and integrated error history
legacy_cells.BI: Models A–D; reduced-order Neural ODE (NODE) framework
legacy_cells.BN: Mechanistic growth update based on elastic stretch minus critical stretch; anisotropic hyperelastic GOH skin material model; displacement represented by POD
legacy_cells.BS: Reconstructed full displacement field via POD; mechanistically updated growth fields; final integrated scalar area gain
legacy_cells.BV: One-step latent-state MSE; long-horizon tail smooth-L1 loss; final integrated area-gain relative-error penalty; capped and weighted rollout loss
legacy_cells.DQ: 1,000 generated Abaqus simulations; 927 converged; 742 training and 185 validation simulations
legacy_cells.DX: Best validation one-step latent MSE: Model A 1.56 × 10⁻³; B 1.29 × 10⁻³; C 1.39 × 10⁻³; D 1.14 × 10⁻³
legacy_cells.DY: Autoregressive rollout displacement RMSE assessed over time through 98.0 days; final area-gain cases within tolerance: A 43.7%, B 53.5%, C 33.5%, D 90.3%
legacy_cells.EG: Model D mean inference runtime 0.151 ± 0.0341 seconds per simulation on 4 AMD Epyc Milan cores; reported as over 20,000× faster than corresponding Abaqus simulations
legacy_cells.EK: Compared open-loop Model A with scalar area-feedback Model B, POD growth-feedback Model C, and CNN growth-feedback Model D; CNN-feedback Model D had 90.3% of validation cases within final-area-gain tolerance versus 43.7% for Model A.
legacy_cells.EL: Open-loop Model A drifts and under-predicts final area gain; Model C shows prediction instability as rollout time progresses; Model B has high variance and can worsen some displacement trajectories.
legacy_cells.FB: POD-compressed displacement coefficients plus expander volume form the latent state; spatial growth is evolved mechanistically and may be encoded as feedback.
legacy_cells.FL: Displacement-field snapshots are compressed by POD to nine coefficients; these and expander volume form a 10D state; a fully connected Neural ODE advances the state, with optional scalar/POD/CNN-encoded mechanistic growth feedback; POD reconstructs displacement and mechanistic equations update growth; no planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors introduce a Neural ODE reduced-order model for tissue-expansion deformation and growth and compare scalar, POD-based, and CNN-based growth-feature feedback to reduce long-horizon error accumulation.
legacy_cells.FN: On 185 validation simulations, CNN-feedback Model D put 90.3% of final area-gain predictions within the stated tolerance versus 43.7% for open-loop Model A; inference was reported over 20,000× faster than Abaqus.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that more training examples or restricting the final-volume domain may be needed for a clinically usable surrogate; geometry variation and accuracy refinement remain necessary.
legacy_cells.FP: Investigate additional data, patient-specific geometry variation, and model refinements to improve accuracy and advance toward clinical use.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify a gap in reduced-order growth-and-remodeling approaches, which typically interpolate simulation snapshots or regress inputs to outputs rather than learning system-state evolution.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is simulation-only: validation uses held-out Abaqus-generated cases, not patient outcomes or external clinical data. The paper does not establish treatment-effect identification, counterfactual validity, clinical utility, or planning/control performance; its speed and tolerance results are surrogate-to-simulator evidence.
